goal: Compare the five most popular open-source vector databases for a small startup.

children.title: Pick the five databases
children.instructions: Name the five most popular open-source vector databases, judged by GitHub stars, community adoption and production use. Only include databases whose core is available under an open-source licence. Return names only, one per item.

template.title: Research {{item}}
template.instructions: Summarise {{item}} for a small startup. Cover: licence, self-hosting and managed hosting options, key features (index types, filtering, hybrid search, scaling), strengths, weaknesses, rough cost at 1-10M vectors for self-hosted and managed, operational effort, and ecosystem or client library maturity. Flag any figure you are unsure of.

children.title: Write the comparison and recommendation
children.instructions: Produce the final deliverable. Lead with a short answer: which database a small startup should pick by default and a runner-up. Then give a tight comparison table of the five databases (licence, hosting options, scale, features, cost at 1-10M vectors, operational effort), followed by a brief note on each one's best fit and main risk, and a short section on when the recommendation would change. State uncertainty where the research flagged it.
